vocabulary.definition: The result of multiplying a number by 1, 2, 3, and so on — where you land when you skip-count by it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El resultado de multiplicar un número por 1, 2, 3, y así sucesivamente: donde caes al contar de esa cantidad.

vocabulary.definition: The largest number that is a factor of two or more numbers. It answers “how many equal groups can I make?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número más grande que es factor de dos o más números. Responde “¿cuántos grupos iguales puedo formar?”
vocabulary.cloze: The largest number that divides both is their ___ ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. It answers “when will these line up again?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número más pequeño que es múltiplo de dos o más números. Responde “¿cuándo volverán a coincidir?”
vocabulary.cloze: The smallest number both numbers reach is their ___ ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: Two factors that multiply to make a number. In a word problem, one is the number of groups and the other is the size of each group.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos factores que se multiplican para formar un número. En un problema, uno es la cantidad de grupos y el otro el tamaño de cada grupo.
vocabulary.cloze: Two factors that multiply to make the number are a ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: Writing a number as a product of prime numbers, usually with a factor tree. Multiplying the primes two numbers share also gives the GCF.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir un número como producto de números primos, normalmente con un árbol de factores. Multiplicar los primos que dos números comparten también da el MCD.
vocabulary.cloze: Writing a number as ___ numbers multiplied together is its prime factorization.

copyPanel.rule: Greatest Common Factor (GCF) & Least Common Multiple (LCM)
steps: 1. GCF: Largest factor shared by two numbers — used to simplify fractions or divide into equal groups
2. LCM: Smallest shared multiple — used to find common denominators
3. Use prime factor trees or list method to find common factors/multiples

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Party Plans
revealWordProblem.text: Reginald is having hot dogs at his party, and 24 people are coming. His mom wants the same number of hot dogs and buns, with none left over. Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns come in packs of 8. How many packs of each should they buy, and how many hot dogs and buns will they have?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A pack of hot dogs labeled 10 count beside a pack of hot dog buns labeled 8 count.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Nothing is being split into groups here — packs are being counted forward until the two totals match — so this is a least-common-multiple problem. Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40 …. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40 …. The first total both pack sizes reach exactly is 40, so the LCM of 10 and 8 is 40. That means 4 packs of hot dogs (4 × 10 = 40) and 5 packs of buns (5 × 8 = 40), giving 40 of each with none left over — more than enough for 24 guests. Any smaller number of packs would leave some hot dogs without buns.

reviewCheck.stem: Using prime factors, 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 and 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. What is their GCF?
reviewCheck.explanation: Take only the primes both numbers have: two 2s and one 3. Multiplying them gives 2 × 2 × 3 = 12, matching the answer from the factor lists.
choiceFeedback: Multiplying every prime from both trees gives a common multiple, not a common factor.
Both numbers have TWO 2s in common, not one — so the 6 is short a factor of 2.
2 is shared, but 48 and 36 each contain two 2s and a 3, so more is shared than that.
hints: Circle the primes that appear in BOTH trees.
48 has four 2s and one 3; 36 has two 2s and two 3s.
Take the smaller count of each shared prime, then multiply.
reviewCheck.stemEs: Usando factores primos, 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 y 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. ¿Cuál es su MCD?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: Toma solo los primos que ambos números tienen: dos 2 y un 3. Al multiplicarlos da 2 × 2 × 3 = 12, igual que la respuesta de las listas de factores.
hintsEs: Encierra los primos que aparecen en AMBOS árboles.
48 tiene cuatro 2 y un 3; 36 tiene dos 2 y dos 3.
Toma la menor cantidad de cada primo compartido y luego multiplica.
